import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 184

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/184](https://www.erdosproblems.com/184)
- [BM22] Bucić, M. and Montgomery, R., Towards the Erdős-Gallai Cycle Decomposition Conjecture.
  arXiv:2211.07689 (2022).
- [CFS14] Conlon, David and Fox, Jacob and Sudakov, Benny, Cycle packing. Random Structures
  Algorithms (2014), 608-626.
- [EGP66] Erdős, Paul and Goodman, A. W. and Pósa, Lajos, The representation of a graph by set
  intersections. Canadian J. Math. (1966), 106-112.
- [Er71] Erdős, P., Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis. Combinatorial
  Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
-/

open Filter SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos184

/--
A graph $H$ is a cycle or an edge if it is connected and 2-regular, or if it has exactly one edge.
-/
def IsCycleOrEdge {U : Type*} [Fintype U] (H : SimpleGraph U) : Prop :=
  open scoped Classical in
  (H.Connected ∧ H.IsRegularOfDegree 2) ∨ H.edgeFinset.card = 1

open scoped Classical in
/--
Any graph on $n$ vertices can be decomposed into $O(n)$ many edge-disjoint cycles and edges.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_184 :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ,
      (f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧
        IsDecomposition G D ∧
        (D.card : ℝ) ≤ f (Fintype.card V) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
Erdős and Gallai [EGP66] proved that $O(n \log n)$ many cycles and edges suffices.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_184.variants.n_log_n :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ,
      (f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧
        IsDecomposition G D ∧
        (D.card : ℝ) ≤ f (Fintype.card V) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
The graph $K_{3,n-3}$ shows that at least $(1+c)n$ many cycles and edges are required, for some
constant $c>0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_184.variants.lower_bound :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
      let G : SimpleGraph (Fin n) := fromRel (fun (i j : Fin n) => (i : ℕ) < 3 ∧ 3 ≤ (j : ℕ));
      ∀ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) →
        IsDecomposition G D →
        (1 + c) * (n : ℝ) ≤ (D.card : ℝ) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
In [Er71] Erdős suggests that only $n-1$ many cycles and edges are required if we do not
require them to be edge-disjoint.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_184.variants.covering :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧
        (⋃ H ∈ D, H.edgeSet) = G.edgeSet ∧
        (D.card : ℝ) ≤ (Fintype.card V : ℝ) - 1 := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
The best bound available is due to Bucić and Montgomery [BM22], who prove that $O(n\log^* n)$ many
cycles and edges suffice, where $\log^*$ is the iterated logarithm function.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_184.variants.bucic_montgomery :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ,
      (f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) * (Real.iteratedLog (n : ℝ) : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧
        IsDecomposition G D ∧
        (D.card : ℝ) ≤ f (Fintype.card V) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov [CFS14] proved that $O_\epsilon(n)$ cycles and edges suffice if $G$ has
minimum degree at least $\epsilon n$, for any $\epsilon>0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_184.variants.conlon_fox_sudakov :
    ∀ ε > 0, ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ,
      (f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      (G.minDegree : ℝ) ≥ ε * (Fintype.card V : ℝ) →
      ∃ (D : Finset G.Subgraph),
        (∀ H ∈ D, IsCycleOrEdge H.coe) ∧
        IsDecomposition G D ∧
        (D.card : ℝ) ≤ f (Fintype.card V) := by
  sorry

end Erdos184

status_issues.source_status: Solved affirmatively by L. Pyber in 1985: every n-vertex graph can be covered by at most n−1 cycles and edges.
status_issues.evidence: Pyber, An Erdős–Gallai conjecture, Combinatorica 5 (1985), 67–79, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF02579444. Its abstract states: “The following conjecture of P. Erdős and T. Gallai is confirmed: every graph on n vertices can be covered by n−1 circuits and edges.” Both cited papers, BM22 and CFS14, explicitly describe this covering result as proved by Pyber.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to research solved, replace answer(sorry) with answer(True), and update the docstring and references to cite Pyber's result. The right-hand mathematical statement needs no change.

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement uses an existential real-valued upper-bound function f with f = O(n), rather than directly giving a uniform constant C with at most Cn pieces.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n ≥ 1, a big-O bound on a function on ℕ gives a positive C with |f(n)| ≤ Cn for every such n, absorbing the finitely many exceptions into C. Consequently D.card ≤ f(n) implies D.card ≤ Cn. At n = 0 the empty decomposition suffices. Conversely, a uniform Cn bound supplies f(n) = Cn. This universe-polymorphic equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean without invoking the conjecture.

reformulations.difference: Cycles are represented as finite connected 2-regular graphs. A one-edge piece is allowed to carry isolated vertices, rather than being required to have exactly two vertices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A finite connected 2-regular simple graph is exactly a single simple cycle. For a one-edge piece, deleting isolated vertices preserves its edge set. In an edge-disjoint decomposition this also preserves the number of pieces, because distinct pieces cannot have the same nonempty edge set. In a covering, any duplicates created by this deletion can be removed, only decreasing the number of pieces. Thus these conventions leave every problem statement in the file unchanged.

reformulations.difference: Real.iteratedLog iterates the natural logarithm, whereas Bucić–Montgomery's Notation section specifies logarithms to base 2.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The stopping times L_e(x) and L_2(x), both stopping at a value ≤ 1, satisfy L_e(x) ≤ L_2(x) ≤ L_e(x) + 2 for x > 1, by comparison of their iterated-exponential thresholds. Since L_e(n) ≥ 1 for n ≥ 2, n L_e(n) and n L_2(n) are Θ-equivalent and give exactly the same big-O assertion. The scratch file also proves that the set defining Real.iteratedLog is nonempty, so its sInf does not take an unintended empty-set default.

review.notes: Checked the helper and all six theorems against the cited sources. The main problem remains open according to the source; the other solved tags agree with the literature. Lean checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean cover empty graphs, one-edge and cycle examples, minimum-degree boundaries, the K_{3,n−3} adjacency relation, the covering bound's real subtraction, and termination of iterated logarithms. Both scratch.lean and equivalence.lean compile without errors; the named verification proofs have no sorryAx dependency. Exact enumeration additionally checked small graph decompositions through six vertices and the covering bound through five vertices. The reviewed file's Git object hash matches the specified commit.
